documents_checked.text:
When students use AI repeatedly and authentically in learning tasks, they build their ability to judge when AI is
useful, evaluate what it produces, and experience what it means to remain accountable for the final work. When
coupled with learning and assessment designs that ask students to explain how and why they used AI, and to clarify
their own contribution to AI-augmented work, AI-integrated learning can nurture academic integrity behaviours by
rewarding transparency, honesty and accountability. Making these behaviours more visible also means educators
are positioned to guide students’ decision-making, provide feedback on their AI use, and assess not only what
students produce, but how responsibly they arrived there.

appropriately weighted (typically at least 20% of the final Unit mark). Any Mandatory
Assessment Task must not be a group task unless approved by the relevant Associate Dean

documents_checked.text:
Each Unit Coordinator is required to promote academic integrity through supporting an
educational approach in the design and delivery of Unit curriculum, assessment, and feedback
aligned to the Academic Quality and Standards of the University, including:
when Courses and Units are developed or reviewed, integrating the use of enabling
technologies, learning and assessment experiences that allow Students to develop and
demonstrate good academic practices as they progress through a Course or Unit;
ensuring that Students are aware of and demonstrate acknowledgement and referencing
practices that apply to each Assessment; and
reporting on assessment practices and outcomes to their relevant Assessment Panel or Unit
Review Committee, as applicable in accordance with the Assessment Panel Procedures.

dimensions.reason: N090 requires annual consolidated academic integrity reporting to Unit Review Committees and Academic Board, School action plans, and regular policy review.

documents_checked.text:
provide an annual consolidated report on academic integrity within the University, to each Unit
Review Committee and to the Academic Board; and
maintain and secure confidential records of academic integrity allegations, breaches,
investigations and outcomes, in accordance with the University’s Privacy Policy, Records
Management Policy and any other applicable law.
Each School will respond to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Students and Education)’s annual
report, for submission to Academic Board, addressing the following in relation to their School
or Teaching Area:
data and trends relating to concerns, allegations and findings of Academic Breach and
Academic Misconduct for Students;
the manner in which allegations were dealt with;
the steps taken to promote academic integrity and to minimise Academic Breach and
Academic Misconduct; and
action plans to continuously improve academic integrity.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Attributable human/group responsibility and traceable disclosure of relevant AI assistance. Access differences become critical where a required tool blocks participation without a workable alternative.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N090 requires proper acknowledgement and own work, N154 mandates individual achievement verification for major group tasks and Fair Assessment, and no required AI tool blocks participation here.
case_summary.case_note: ECU governs group assessment through N154 individual-contribution verification for tasks over 30 percent and N090 acknowledgement and own-work obligations. Although no group-level AI tracking mechanism is prescribed, attributable responsibility is preserved and no mandatory tool blocks equitable access. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review.

supporting_passages.text:
This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.
